---
title: "Outline"
subtitle: "Six chapters, in the order they will be taught"
---

The course is organised into six chapters. The first two explore why insurance exists and how insurance contracts are designed. The middle chapters turn to pricing and aggregate-loss modelling, while the final two focus on risk measurement and dependence between risks.

::: {.syllabus}

1. ### [The history of insurance and the role of mathematics](./history.html)

   A brief historical introduction to insurance, from informal forms of mutual aid and early maritime risk sharing to the development of organised insurance markets. We will see how marine insurance gradually became distinct from credit and trade finance, how institutions such as Lloyd's and fire insurers emerged, and how life assurance, reinsurance, social insurance and compulsory insurance developed over time. Particular attention will be paid to the interaction between practice and mathematics: insurance existed long before probability theory, but the development of probability, mortality tables, the law of large numbers and later actuarial and extreme-value methods progressively changed the way risks could be measured and managed. Conversely, some mathematical developments were themselves driven by concrete insurance and risk-management problems.

2. ### [Microeconomics of insurance](./micro.html)

   We begin with preferences over risky wealth and their representation by expected utility. Certainty equivalents and risk premia lead to the Arrow–Pratt measures of risk aversion and the comparison of different attitudes towards risk, with CARA and CRRA utility as central examples. We then study the demand for insurance: how willingness to pay depends on loss probability, loss size and wealth, and how a safety loading affects optimal proportional coverage. Mossin’s theorem explains why full insurance is not optimal under a positive loading. Finally, under pricing proportional to the expected indemnity, we prove the optimality of deductible contracts and reduce the choice of insurance to the choice of a deductible.
